title: HIGH: bbox-cull (task 1327) REORDERS top-wins z between untouched and merged shapes — drops existing↔existing cut
description:
REGRESSION introduced by 41a7646 (task 1327 "bbox-cull the planar merge fold"). The perf cull CHANGES the geometric result.

ROOT CAUSE (exact diff): packages/core/src/engine/planar/merge.ts:287 planarMergeCommit now returns [...passthrough, ...untouched, mergedObj] (was [...passthrough, mergedObj] pre-cull). The cull (foldShapeIntoLayerCulled, merge.ts:211) splits the layer's mergeable shapes into 'overlapping' (folded into mergedObj) and 'untouched' (re-emitted as separate display objects). It re-emits ALL untouched shapes BELOW the merged object, destroying their original draw-order relative to shapes that got pulled into the merge.

WHY WRONG: the merge model is top-wins / draw-order-dependent (per CLAUDE.md and docs/36). When two EXISTING mergeable shapes overlap each other and only the EARLIER-drawn one overlaps the incoming stroke, the earlier shape is folded into mergedObj while the LATER-drawn shape is marked 'untouched'. The later shape SHOULD win their mutual overlap (it was drawn on top), but planarMergeCommit puts mergedObj ON TOP of untouched -> the overlap flips color. The cull's correctness comment (merge.ts:197-209) only reasons about edges crossing the INCOMING stroke; it ignores existing↔existing interactions that the pre-cull single-arrangement fold resolved correctly.

PRE-CULL was correct: foldShapeIntoLayer(mergeable, incoming) folded ALL mergeable shapes into ONE kernel arrangement in draw order, so every mergeable↔mergeable overlap resolved in-kernel with correct top-wins. The cull's untouched-partition breaks this. It ALSO breaks the prior invariant that a keyframe holds at most one merged mergeable shape after each commit — now untouched shapes accumulate as separate display objects, making the bug reachable on the 2nd commit onward and via FLA import / paste / route-all-paths (task 1328) populating a keyframe with many mergeable shapes.

MINIMAL FAILING INPUT (verified, scratch test removed):
  existing (draw order bottom->top): eBLUE rect[50..80,30..50] BLUE; eRED rect[40..70,20..40] RED (drawn LATER, overlaps eBLUE in [50..70,30..40]=area 200)
  incoming: GREEN rect[30..66,45..60] (overlaps eBLUE only; y>=45 misses eRED)
  EXPECTED (full/pre-cull fold, draw order): BLUE area=320 (eBLUE minus eRED-on-top overlap minus green), RED=full, GREEN=full
  ACTUAL (culled planarMergeCommit): BLUE area=520 (eRED is untouched, re-emitted BELOW merged eBLUE -> eBLUE wins the [50..70,30..40] overlap that eRED should win). Divergence = 200 area units, RED->BLUE color flip.
  Same defect surfaced in a 60-trial randomized fuzz (trial 50: RED full=1802 vs culled=1634, BLUE full=1145 vs culled=1313).

REPRO: fold the layer through planarMergeCommit and compare per-color face area (z-order-respecting buildArrangementFromShapes on the result in draw order) vs foldShapeIntoLayer(all mergeable, incoming). Areas diverge by the existing↔existing overlap.

FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) the cull must also include any untouched shape that overlaps an OVERLAPPING shape (transitive overlap closure), not just shapes overlapping the incoming; OR (b) preserve relative z between untouched and merged by re-emitting per original index rather than a flat [untouched, merged] split; OR (c) only cull shapes that are disjoint from ALL participating geometry. The pre-cull whole-layer fold is the correctness reference.

NOT defects (verified): curve bbox extent is correct — edgeBBox (geometry.ts:164) computes quadratic extrema incl. the bulge (a y=200 endpoints / control y=160 curve bbox minY=180, the true bulge, not endpoint 200 nor control 160); cull predicate boundsOverlap (merge.ts:139) is conservative with +1px tolerance (touching/corner cases included). Perf claim holds: 400 dense fills, stroke touching one -> full 46ms vs culled 0.30ms (155x), 399 culled out; not a no-op.

UNAFFECTED: golden-parity exit 0, hash STILL 9d09912df4727d0c (golden has no multi-mergeable-shape merge layer). All planar guards pass (planar 30, eraser 14, adversarial 20, subselection 14, planar-merge 11) — none cover the multi-mergeable-shape z-order case, which is the coverage gap that let this through. A regression test should author 2+ overlapping mergeable shapes (later one outside the incoming stroke bbox) and assert culled == whole-layer fold.
